paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the door is OPEN. Jesus offered one sacrifice, so the writer says we have "confidence to enter the Most Holy Place by the blood of Jesus" (Hebrews 10:19). We have "a great priest over the house of God," so we're told, "let us draw near with a sincere heart in full assurance of faith" (Hebrews 10:21-22). Don't hover in the doorway like somebody who thinks the invitation was a typo!

So how do we stay near? The writer says to "hold resolutely to the hope we profess, for He who promised is faithful" and to spur one another on to "love and good deeds," not neglecting meeting together (Hebrews 10:23-25). Then comes a heavy warning: if we deliberately go on sinning after receiving the knowledge of the truth, "no further sacrifice for sins remains, but only a fearful expectation of judgment" (Hebrews 10:26-27). The writer asks how much more severely one deserves to be punished who has trampled on the Son of God, and says it is "a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God" (Hebrews 10:29, 31).

Then comes the call to persevere. The writer says, "So do not throw away your confidence; it holds a great reward" (Hebrews 10:35). These believers had already lost property and still held on, because they knew they had "a better and permanent possession" (Hebrews 10:34). And the writer says, "we are not of those who shrink back and are destroyed, but of those who have faith and preserve their souls" (Hebrews 10:39). So come near, baker, keep holding on, and keep your ovens ready, because He who is coming "will not delay" (Hebrews 10:37).
